author: buchanan_robert
text:
A little baby, all shy and frail,
 Comes down to the water's edge so pale;
  The breeze that blew o’er the sea,

 The wind-voice on his ear it made,
 And made him weep as he hid his face.

author: cushag
text:
'In the garden where flowers bloom,
My friend and I play under the dome,
Under the sky with all its blue,

Where we can shout and sing like doves
And laugh till our faces get dry;
And when it gets dusk and the day is done,
We go home at twilight to tea and buns.'

Haiku is not considered to be poetry, but rather as a form of prose and it is generally written as a single sentence consisting of three lines:

Line 1 has five syllables
Line 2 has seven syllables
And line 3 has five syllable

The subject of haiku may range from nature to an everyday occurrence such as cooking or walking home from work.

author: buchanan_robert
text: In this world we will never escape death. Like a beautiful flower that eventually withers away, we too are only here for some time. We should enjoy our life as much as possible while we can because sooner or later our time will be up. In this case, I think this is what my poem should represent. The birds are probably referring to us humans.

author: cushag
text:
In the street, where many a man has gone
To see his wife and children by her friend,
And come back to say "I've seen 'em both, they're fine";

Where I have found so many an old-time mate;
A few who look like brothers as they pass--
God bless them! God bless them all that way!

The streets are full of sights: how can you stay?
As one goes down the street and sees it go up again,
It must be awful when you lose your ship at sea!

author: emily_dickinson
text:
A song to the memory of my mother:

The last hour she lay by my side;
 I watched her white lips for a smile,
 And saw them draw apart like mist
 As on the day that she was born;
 The soft, dark eyes that were not blind
 Had closed with sleep; and the cold breast
 That had no milk for me at first
 Was motionless as stone or ice.

Sepia tone, a mixture of red and blue, is created by mixing equal amounts of cyan (blue-green) and yellow inks on paper. As you can see from Figure 23.18, when an object appears to be green or blue under a black light it has absorbed both the blue and red primary colors (i.e., cyan and yellow). A person wearing a shirt that was painted with this dye would appear sepia under black light since neither the red nor the blue wavelengths are being reflected off the surface. Answer: The sepia ink absorbs both

author: cushag
text:
Johnnie and Me Were Married
By William WordsworthMy husband, John, and I were married many years ago. We had several children; it’s amazing to see how quickly they have grown! Now my son-in-law comes along with his little daughter and says, “Mary, Mary, hurry up,” while my daughter asks, “John, John will you come and help me.” And I am spending my time washing dishes, and John is always going off for more food.

Vasilii Zhukovsky, "Spring" (1810)

The sun is already warming on earth,
And in heaven he shines through all night...
Dances over the forest -
As if a bright fairy tale!

Trees are covered with foliage -
They were so tired last winter;
Now they've slept enough:
What joy to shine again !

A song from a bird-spring,
I heard somewhere in the field:
“All good things come true!
Come and wake up spring ! “

author: robert_frost
text:
'A King and a Cow,' we hear,
A king went out to see;
He saw some black-and-white cows,
As he rode on his gee.'

But who were they that gave him this pleasure?
They were the kings of old--they were the sons of gold.

author: robert_frost
text: He knows all too well he’ll end up being jobless once more. He keeps going from one job to another but ends up returning home empty-handed. The next day, you see him roaming around asking for alms as if nothing had happened just then. It appears that he has been deceived by the owner of the place where he worked last time about not paying him wages and hence now needs money desperately. But do we need to tell him how wrong he is or leave things as they are? It seems better not to interfere with whatever happens between them.

Haiku is a traditional Japanese form of poetry. It consists of three lines, with 5 syllables in the first line, 7 in the second and 5 again in the third. This creates an almost musical effect as the reader moves through it.

This haiku captures the way that time passes so quickly:

It’s nearly lunchtime now
and I don’t have enough hours left to do anything else
I’m going to make myself busy!

Persian (Old)

The old Persian language, also known as Old Iranian or Old Avestan, is an ancient Indo-Iranian language that was spoken and written by Zoroastrians from about 1500 BCE to about 200 CE. It is one of the oldest attested forms of the Indo-European family of languages, along with Hittite and Sanskrit.

Old Persian developed from Proto-Indo-Iranian around 1400–1300 BC as part of the division into Old Iranian (or East Iranian), which gave rise to modern Persian

A breeze I feel, like rain,
And flowers blooming on branches
Like buds are opening in spring

My soul feels peace within
Where love shines brightly from above.

author: william_wordsworth
text:
Oh, bright star of the evening, splendor of the west,
Star of my country, resting upon the horizon,
You are like a majestic figure hanging over England' s bosom,
Your beauty shines brightly while resting beneath your own stars,
Blessings be unto you both, sharing one goal and one fate,
May prosperity fill your hearts, my dear nation,
I long for you from afar, waiting for our return together.
